title: Burst-sensitive probabilistic sampler to cut hotpath tracing cost
creator: Priya Desai
description:
Problem: Tracing instrumentation currently imposes a measurable CPU and allocation tax on hot RPC paths during short client microbursts. Existing probabilistic samplers make per-request decisions and sometimes allocate small objects on the hot path, increasing p50/p95 CPU and amplifying tail latency under bursty traffic.

Objective: Reduce hotpath overhead of sampling to under 0.5% CPU at p50 for high-QPS routes while preserving capture rate for tail/error traces (p99 error detection). Implement a burst-sensitive probabilistic sampler that minimizes allocations and synchronisation on the hot path and moves heavier bookkeeping to an async commit path.

Proposal (high level):
- Two-stage sampling decision: 1) a microburst-prefilter in the hot path implemented in C++ (tracing hook) that uses a lock-free per-route burst counter + leaky-bucket estimate to quickly accept obvious samples or early-exit; 2) for uncertain cases, mark a lightweight hint and enqueue to an async sampler-reservoir worker for final probabilistic accept/commit.
- Hotpath constraints: no heap allocations, use stack scratch space and per-thread ring-slot to avoid mutexes; decision must be <200ns median additional cost on the path.
- Async reservoir: a background shard-per-core worker keeps a bounded reservoir (reservoir size configurable per-tenant/route) and periodically emits sampled traces to the collector. It performs reservoir decay and tail-promotion logic to prioritize long-running/error-prone traces.
- Tail reconstruction: when a trace is accepted by async reservoir, a compact trace-hint (trace-id + short TTL + route shard) triggers on-collector rehydration to fetch associated KV cache prefixes and span summaries to reconstruct context for debugging/eval.

Trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive early-exit reduces overhead but risks missing rare error tails; mitigated by reservoir tail-promotion and route-specific override rules for error-only sampling.
- Per-route state increases memory footprint; we coalesce low-traffic routes into a fallback bucket to bound memory.
- Async commit adds eventual consistency: sampled traces may appear later; dashboarding and alerts will use the commit timestamp to avoid confusion.

Acceptance criteria (prototype):
- Hotpath allocation reduction: new sampler must show zero heap allocations in the hot path for sampled/non-sampled requests (validated via pprof).
- CPU overhead: end-to-end CPU overhead attributable to tracing hooks reduced from current +3-7% to <0.5% at p50 on benchmark harness for target routes.
- Tail capture: for synthetic error injection tests, tail/error trace capture rate >= 95% compared to baseline when using default route/tenant configs.
- No regression on request latency SLOs (p99 request latency must not regress by >1%).

Implementation plan (milestones):
1) Benchmark harness and microbench (week 1): add synthetic burst scenarios; baseline current sampler performance (cpu, allocations, latency).
2) Hotpath prefilter implementation (week 2): C++ change in tracing hook; unit tests + allocation checks.
3) Async reservoir worker (week 3): golang worker with sharded queues and reservoir decay logic; config knobs per-route.
4) Integration + synthetic tail tests (week 4): inject long-running/error traces, compare capture rates.
5) Canary rollout (week 5): route-level canary on low-traffic region (eu-west-2) with dashboards and auto-rollback trigger.
6) Gradual rollout and observability: global rollout with per-tenant tuning and runbook.

Rollout and monitoring plan:
- Dashboards: trace-sampler/hotpath-cost, trace-sampler/async-queue-latency, trace-sampler/tail-capture-rate. Initial dashboards at https://console.redwood.internal/dashboards/trace-sampler (internal).
- Metrics emitted: sampler.hotpath_ns, sampler.hotpath_allocs, sampler.async_queue_depth, sampler.reservoir_size, sampler.tail_promotion_rate, sampler.missed_error_traces.
- Canary watchlist: sampler hotpath_ns, p95 CPU, p99 request latency, tail_capture_rate < 90% triggers rollback.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc (internal): https://docs.redwood.internal/observability/sampling/burst-sensitive-sampler.md
- Benchmark harness (repo): https://github.com/redwood/inference/tree/main/bench/sampler-harness
- WIP PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/7890
- Perf comparison dashboard (snapshot): https://console.redwood.internal/dashboards/snapshots/ENG-125678-perf-2025-02-28

Open decisions:
- Default reservoir size per tenant: conservative default 200, allow enterprise override. (Action: product to confirm).
- Tenant opt-in model vs global rollout: initial plan is tenant opt-in for Dedicated/Private customers; hosted default off for first canary. (Action: PM to confirm).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: background queue backlog under extreme surge could delay tail capture. Mitigation: bounded queue with backpressure metrics, emergency bypass mode to switch to direct-sample for error-only traces.
- Risk: incorrect per-route coalescing may bias sampling. Mitigation: include periodic route-cardinality audits and default route-map heuristics.

Next steps (short term):
- Complete hotpath microbench PR and get code review from @Aisha Raman and @Jon Park.
- Product to confirm reservoir defaults and opt-in policy by 2025-02-18.
- Setup canary dashboard and alert runbooks before 2025-03-01.
